newsitem.title: PERU: Peru oil workers held by rebels said out safely.
newsitem.headline: Peru oil workers held by rebels said out safely.

text.p: A group of Peruvian oil workers believed held in the central jungle by the Maoist Shining Path movement have all returned safely, an official at the workers' company said.

"They are all out now. They are all out of the bush. It's over," the official at Peru's Compania General de Geofisica (CGG), who asked not to be identified, told Reuters in a telephone interview from the jungle town of Satipo. He would not give more details immediately.
An Interior Ministry spokesman in Lima, processing information from police in the zone, confirmed that the approximately 29 oil workers had been released unharmed by the rebels.

Contrasting with earlier information from police and military sources in the zone, the spokesman said the rebels had only held the men for four hours on Friday. They forced the men to listen to ideological talks, and stole food, medicine and communications equipment from their camp.
About 300 police and army soldiers were searching for the estimated 50- to 60-strong guerrilla patrol, the ministry spokesman added. "It seems we are getting close," he said.
The CGG was carrying out exploration work for French oil company Elf.
